summary: Reviewed Enterprise, SAM Coupe, Thomson, Oric, CoCo and SourceGen discovery leads
notes: Queue work rechecked the SourceGen Apple II pages and geogeo28 Atari ST project tree. Fresh-search routes and exact queries: web/GitHub repository search — site:github.com Thomson MO5 TO7 TO8 disassembly reconstruction source; site:github.com Oric Atmos disassembly reassembly source reconstruction; site:github.com Atari Lynx disassembly reassembly decompilation source; site:github.com TRS-80 Color Computer CoCo disassembly reconstruction tooling; site:github.com Enterprise 128 disassembly source reconstruction; site:github.com SAM Coupe disassembly source reconstruction; site:github.com Sharp X1 disassembly source reconstruction; site:github.com Dragon 32 disassembly source reconstruction. Eleven candidate URLs were screened; six were promoted, two deferred, and three SourceGen collection pages resolved to existing tracked projects. The CPU audit queue returned zero unresolved areas before selection, so no existing CPU fields were refreshed merely to satisfy a quota.

sources.reason: Historical AZAS/MINI-DOS source, bootable disk images and AZA86 conversion tooling for NEC and Sharp Z80 systems.
SAM Coupe graphics conversion and sprite-specific Z80 code-generation tool.
VS Code build, run and deployment integration for SAM Coupe Z80 projects.
Enterprise 128 C-development library and crt0 for SDCC's Z80 backend.
Maintained MiSTer FPGA core and associated Oric media/snapshot analysis tools.
Video conversion pipeline and native 6809 player for Thomson MO/TO computers.
Archived GitHub mirror of a CoCo OS-9/BASIC 6809 disassembler now pointing to a GitLab canonical repository.
Dragon/6809 ROM-information candidate returned by fresh search but unavailable at review time.

source_updates.reason: Rechecked the Apple II ROM, GS/OS FST and RDOS pages; the latter two and the independently qualified ROM components are already tracked, while the broader outbound disassembly graph remains open.
Rechecked the current projects tree: it still contains the six tracked Atari ST reconstruction subjects plus the previously excluded original homebrew BLACK ICE, with no new title directory.

task_updates.notes_append: Rechecked the Apple II ROM, GS/OS FST and RDOS landing pages. GS/OS and RDOS are already tracked; the mixed ROM index is already split into its independently qualified projects. No duplicate collection record was added; outbound links remain to review.

Rechecked the repository project tree; no new reverse-engineering target has appeared beyond the six tracked Atari ST projects, and BLACK ICE remains original homebrew rather than an RE-derived project.

project.title: AZAS / MINI-DOS
project.display_title: AZAS / MINI-DOS — preserved Z80 development system

runtime_profiles.name: PC-8001 ROM 1.1 with MULTICARD
runtime_profiles.notes: The README states this specific PC-8001 configuration; it is not generalized to the PC-8801 or Sharp X1 variants.

project.status: Historical source and bootable disk images preserved; not independently executed

identity.narrative: The primary README identifies a preserved AZAS assembler, SOCE editor, MINI-DOS and bootable D88 images for PC-8001/8801 and Sharp X1.

classification.narrative: This is historical original-source preservation and development tooling, not a binary-derived reconstruction. AZA86 additionally translates AZAS Z80 source for MASM on 8086 systems.

source_cpu.narrative: The preserved native development system and assembler sources target Z80 programs; this is the original architecture rather than a host minimum.

target_cpu.narrative: AZAS produces Z80 work, while the documented AZA86 conversion route translates AZAS Z80 source to MASM 8086 form.

build.narrative: Source and bootable D88 images are present, but no clean build or execution was performed. Build, run and byte-identity flags remain unknown.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The README explicitly requires 64 KB, ROM 1.1 and MULTICARD for its PC-8001 configuration. No equivalent minimum was stated for the PC-8801 or Sharp X1 variants.

ai.narrative: No development-AI attribution was found in the inspected primary README or pinned head commit; non-use is not inferred.

relationships.narrative: The README presents AZAS, SOCE, MINI-DOS and AZA86 as components of one period development system, so they are curated as one coherent record.

project.title: tile2sam
project.display_title: tile2sam — SAM Coupe graphics and Z80 sprite-code generator
project.status: Install and generation workflow documented; not independently executed

identity.narrative: The pinned README identifies tile2sam as a Python command that converts images into SAM Coupe graphics data or optimized sprite-specific Z80 routines.

classification.narrative: This is directly useful retro-development asset and code-generation tooling, with SAM screen-mode, palette, tile and timing support.

source_cpu.narrative: Input is modern image data rather than a legacy binary with an original CPU architecture.

target_cpu.narrative: The tool explicitly emits Z80 drawing, save, restore, copy and clear routines for SAM Coupe sprites.

build.narrative: The README documents installation through uv and concrete command examples. It was not independently installed or run, so build/run flags remain unknown.

runtime_profiles.narrative: No minimum host CPU or RAM requirement is stated in the inspected documentation.

ai.narrative: No explicit development-AI attribution was found in the pinned README or head commit; non-use is not inferred.

relationships.narrative: The repository and package describe one tool with bundled demos rather than separate independently titled projects.

project.title: vscode-pyz80
project.display_title: vscode-pyz80 — SAM Coupe build, run and deployment extension

runtime_profiles.name: VS Code extension workflow
runtime_profiles.os: Visual Studio Code 1.75+, Python 3.6+, SimCoupe 1.1+; SAMdisk 4 required for network deployment
runtime_profiles.notes: These are documented software prerequisites; no host CPU or RAM minimum is stated.

project.status: Published extension workflow documented; not independently executed

identity.narrative: The README and package manifest identify a VS Code extension for editing and assembling Z80 code for the SAM Coupe.

classification.narrative: It integrates assembly, SAMDOS v2 disk-image creation, SimCoupe launch/symbol maps and optional network delivery to a physical SAM, exceeding syntax highlighting alone.

source_cpu.narrative: The extension is development infrastructure and does not analyze an original legacy binary.

target_cpu.narrative: The documented build workflow invokes pyz80 for SAM Coupe Z80 programs.

build.narrative: The package manifest and README document installation and commands; the extension was not independently installed or executed, so flags remain unknown.

runtime_profiles.narrative: README and package metadata state VS Code 1.75+, Python 3.6+, SimCoupe 1.1+, and SAMdisk 4 for network use. No host CPU or RAM minimum is given.

ai.narrative: No explicit development-AI attribution was found in the inspected README, package manifest or pinned head commit; non-use is not inferred.

relationships.narrative: pyz80, SimCoupe and SAMdisk are external dependencies; this record covers the integration extension itself.

project.title: ep128-devel
project.display_title: ep128-devel — SDCC C library and crt0 for Enterprise 128
project.status: Source reviewed; build and runtime not independently tested

identity.narrative: The root README and sole project directory identify ep128-devel as an Enterprise 128 library and crt0 for SDCC-based C development.

classification.narrative: This is target-specific compiler/runtime infrastructure: wrappers and selected replacements around SDCC's generic Z80 library.

source_cpu.narrative: The library is original development tooling rather than analysis of a legacy binary.

target_cpu.narrative: The README explicitly says the work uses SDCC's Z80 backend and replaces selected generic Z80 routines.

build.narrative: The inspected primary README establishes scope but not a successful reproducible build; no compilation was performed.

runtime_profiles.narrative: No explicit minimum Enterprise CPU variant, RAM, ROM or host requirement was found; none is inferred from the platform name.

ai.narrative: No explicit development-AI attribution was found in the README or pinned head commit; non-use is not inferred.

relationships.narrative: The repository contains one named target project, ep128-devel, which depends on upstream SDCC but is independently scoped Enterprise-specific work.

project.title: Oric_MiSTer
project.display_title: Oric_MiSTer — Oric, Atmos and Pravetz 8D FPGA core

runtime_profiles.name: MiSTer FPGA core
runtime_profiles.notes: The repository targets MiSTer and documents deployed game and launcher paths; no host CPU or RAM minimum is stated. The emulated Oric configuration has 64 KiB RAM, which is not recorded as a MiSTer host minimum.

project.status: Maintained core with checked-in releases; not independently built or run

evidence: Pinned head commit attributes savestate work to Claude Fable 5

identity.narrative: The pinned README identifies the current repository as the MiSTer Oric-1, Oric Atmos and Pravetz 8D FPGA core, with releases and support tools in the same tree.

classification.narrative: The core reimplements ULA video, 6502, VIA, AY sound, keyboard and disk/tape behavior. TAP, SNA and disk tools are supporting parts of the same coherent FPGA project.

source_cpu.narrative: The primary README explicitly identifies the emulated CPU as 6502.

target_cpu.narrative: The output is FPGA logic for MiSTer rather than a port compiled for a documented target CPU.

build.narrative: The README documents the oric-build script and checked-in RBF releases while warning that deployment behavior reflects the maintainer's local setup. No build or execution was independently performed.

runtime_profiles.narrative: MiSTer is the explicit runtime platform. The 64 KiB value describes the emulated Oric RAM, not a minimum host requirement; no MiSTer CPU or RAM minimum is stated.

ai.narrative: The pinned head commit explicitly carries Claude Fable 5 co-author attribution for savestate work, establishing Claude-assisted contribution without generalizing beyond that evidence.

relationships.narrative: The README states this MiSTer core descends from earlier MiST/SiDi Oric FPGA work and used Oricutron source to understand snapshots; those are predecessors/references, not duplicates of the maintained MiSTer tree.

project.title: SDVideo
project.display_title: SDVideo — Thomson MO/TO video converter and 6809 player

runtime_profiles.name: Native SDDrive video player
runtime_profiles.notes: Individual conversion modes have narrower machine compatibility documented in the README; no RAM minimum is stated.

project.status: Converter and player sources reviewed; not independently built or run

identity.narrative: The pinned README and Makefile establish a Lua/FFmpeg conversion pipeline plus native assembly player for SDDrive-equipped Thomson MO/TO machines.

classification.narrative: This is substantial original retro-development tooling: host media conversion and a native player, not reverse engineering of a historical title.

source_cpu.narrative: Input is modern video/audio media rather than a legacy binary with an original CPU.

target_cpu.narrative: The primary documentation explicitly describes a native MC6809 player running at 1 MHz and the repository contains its assembly sources.

build.narrative: The Makefile invokes c6809 and the Lua/FFmpeg tools, but also downloads dependencies and media for test targets. No clean build or run was performed, so flags remain unknown.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The player is explicitly MC6809 at 1 MHz with SDDrive; the README gives per-mode model compatibility. No RAM minimum is stated or inferred.

ai.narrative: No explicit development-AI attribution was found in the README, Makefile or pinned head commit; non-use is not inferred.

relationships.narrative: The converter and native player are documented and built as one SDVideo workflow; no separately titled subproject was established.
